newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance ministry denies tax system report.
newsitem.headline: French finance ministry denies tax system report.

text.p: The French Finance Ministry denied on Thursday a report that a group of European countries including France and Germany was secretly negotiating plans to create a single European tax and social security system.
British daily The Independent reported on Thursday that an alliance of European countries including France and Germany -- but not Britain -- were privately negotiating such a plan.
The newspaper, citing "papers seen by The Independent", said the plan envisaged control over income tax being pooled by national governments inside a future single currency zone.
"We deny it," said a Finance Ministry spokeswoman. "There is no secret agreement between two countries on taxation."
She said any agreement on a common tax system would have to be negotiated by all 15 European Union states.
Earlier, a spokesman at British Prime Minister John Major's office said Britain was not aware of any talks between France and Germany along these lines.
